fichas.title: Outpatient facilities
fichas.summary: Outpatient facilities serve ambulant patients attending by appointment. The design should separate outpatient and inpatient routes, provide rapid access to X-ray, and allow for larger waiting and examination areas where outpatient attendance or day surgery is substantial.
figure_refs: Figure 1: Outpatients, ground floor, Berlin-Spandau Hospital; today: Vivantes Clinic Berlin-Spandau

fichas.title: Outpatient surgery
fichas.summary: Outpatient surgery departments may be added to existing hospitals, integrated with a surgical department, or established as independent clinics. Hospital departments should be near the main entrance and emergency care. A cited elective-treatment arrangement uses smaller operating theatres, a multifunctional preparation room, shared washrooms, a five-place recovery room, and a quiet zone; separate preparation and post-operative rooms, storerooms, and conventional patient access-control lobbies are omitted.

fichas.title: Outpatient medical centre and emergency admission example
fichas.summary: A separate outpatient or short-stay establishment associated with a hospital has room and organisational arrangements distinct from inpatient care. Its medical services and equipment should be assessed for the planned treatment spectrum; furnishing may be more generous regarding hygiene, and ventilation and other technical systems should be critically evaluated. Figure 2 shows an emergency admission plan for Helios Clinic, Gotha, with a waiting room, admissions, examination and treatment spaces, emergency beds, surgery-related rooms, patient changing, and support spaces.
